sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: AWS is the dominant cloud platform for Go backend services, and aws-sdk-go-v2 is the idiomatic way to interact with it. Interviewers at AWS-heavy companies expect you to know the v2 SDK's config loading, service client construction, and context-aware API calls. Lambda, S3, DynamoDB, and SQS are the four services that appear most in Go backend interview problems.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body: aws-sdk-go-v2 is modular: you import only the service packages you need (github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/s3, etc.). Every call requires an aws.Config loaded with config.LoadDefaultConfig(ctx), which resolves credentials via the standard chain: environment variables → ~/.aws/credentials → IAM role for EC2/ECS → IMDS. All API calls are context-aware and return typed result structs and errors. Retries and timeouts are configured on the HTTP client, not globally.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body: 1. config.LoadDefaultConfig: credential chain, WithRegion, WithHTTPClient for custom timeouts; share one config across clients. 2. Lambda Go: lambda.Start(handler), handler signature func(ctx context.Context, event events.APIGatewayProxyRequest) (events.APIGatewayProxyResponse, error), cold-start optimisation (init outside handler). 3. S3: PutObject with context, GetObject streaming with io.ReadAll or io.Copy, presigned URLs with s3.PresignClient. 4. DynamoDB: PutItem/GetItem with attributevalue.MarshalMap, Query with KeyConditionExpression, optimistic locking with ConditionExpression. 5. SQS: SendMessage, ReceiveMessage (long polling WaitTimeSeconds: 20), DeleteMessage after processing, visibility timeout, dead-letter queue. 6. IAM roles: task role for ECS, execution role vs. task role distinction, least-privilege policy. 7. ECS Fargate: task definition, container definition, service with load balancer, TASK_ROLE for SDK auth.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body: • 'How do you authenticate your Go service to AWS in production?' → IAM role attached to ECS task / EC2 instance; SDK picks it up automatically via credential chain; never hardcode access keys. • 'How would you consume SQS messages reliably in Go?' → goroutine pool per message, long polling, delete only after successful processing, dead-letter queue for poison messages. • 'How do you optimise a Go Lambda cold start?' → move SDK client init outside the handler, use graviton2 arm64 for lower cost and faster boot, keep binary small (no CGO). • 'How would you implement a DynamoDB conditional write in Go?' → ConditionExpression with attribute_not_exists(pk) for upsert safety or version number for optimistic locking.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: "I initialise the AWS config once at startup with config.LoadDefaultConfig using a context with a 5-second timeout. In production on ECS I rely entirely on the task IAM role—no static credentials anywhere. For S3 uploads I stream directly from the request body using PutObject with an io.Reader so I never buffer the entire file in memory. SQS consumer is a worker pool: I receive a batch of up to 10 messages with long polling, fan them out to a fixed number of goroutines, and delete each message only after the handler returns nil. For DynamoDB I use attributevalue.MarshalMap to convert Go structs to attribute maps and rely on ConditionExpression for optimistic concurrency control rather than application-level locking."
